add.title: Colorado Department of Corrections (Wikipedia) — Transgender inmates section
add.summary: Wikipedia article (fetched, HTTP 200) whose 'Transgender inmates' section documents the state's actual placement practice: a 2019 class action on behalf of transgender women held in men's prisons alleged CDOC subjected them to sexual and physical violence and denied medically necessary care, and a court-approved 2024 consent decree in Denver District Court (Raven v. Polis) required CDOC to expand health care and create voluntary specialized housing — a 100-bed unit at the men's Sterling facility and an integration unit at the women's prison — and to pay about $2.1 million to roughly 400 class members without admitting liability. It also records a 2019 settlement (Lindsay Saunders-Velez, $170,000) over the safety of a transgender inmate held in a men's prison. Placement axis: no identity-based-housing statute; trans women were historically held in men's prisons, with relief achieved through litigation and consent decree rather than a baseline housing rule.
